spots.s: THE LA date: free telescopes, Art Deco terraces, and the city igniting below as the sun drops — arrive an hour before dusk.
Tram up to Richard Meier's hilltop acropolis — free admission, world-class art, gardens, and 180-degree views that do half the conversational work.
Free contemporary-art heavyweight with the Infinity Mirror Room — book ahead and pair it with Disney Hall across the street.
A century-old downtown market hall where you graze tacos-to-oysters between neon signs — easy, buzzy first-date territory.
Ride the tiny 1901 funicular up Bunker Hill for a dollar — a two-minute time machine that connects straight to Grand Central Market.
Cavernous bank-building bookstore with the famous tunnel of books upstairs — a browse-and-talk date that costs nothing.
Gehry's stainless-steel masterpiece; catch the LA Phil or just walk the free rooftop garden ribboning through the building.
Mochi, sake bars, and 140 years of history in a few walkable blocks — LA's easiest wander-and-snack evening.
Sunset over the San Gabriels, a Dodger Dog, and 50,000 people in a good mood — baseball's best-situated ballpark.
The lamppost forest at dusk is a rite of passage, and the new Geffen Galleries (opened April 2026) finally match the collection.
Movie-history deep dive under a giant glass dome — the Oscars exhibits and rooftop Hollywood Hills view make it a strong rainy-day date.
San Marino's 130-acre wonder — Chinese and Japanese gardens, rose garden, rare books; the single best daytime date in the county.
Camellia forests and oak woodland in La Cañada — quieter than the Huntington, and the winter Enchanted light show is date gold.

spots.n: Santa Monica Pier to Venice walk
spots.s: Classic 2-mile boardwalk stroll from the Ferris wheel to the Venice drum circles — people-watching that never runs out of material.
Abbot Kinney's 1905 canals: footbridges, ducks, and improbable architecture — a quiet golden-hour loop two blocks from the boardwalk chaos.
Malibu's sea-cave and rock-arch cove — scramble down the bluff stairs for the most cinematic sunset picnic in LA county.
The social hike: 2.7 miles of Hollywood ridgeline where half of LA works out — views from the sign to the sea on clear days.

spots.n: Griffith Park Old Zoo & Hollywood sign trails
spots.s: Miles of trails past abandoned 1912 zoo cages up to Hollywood-sign viewpoints — pick your distance, skip the crowds at Runyon.
Bring wine and a picnic box to the world's most famous outdoor stage — summer LA Phil and headliner nights under the stars.
2,500 vendors around the stadium every second Sunday — vintage hunting with built-in conversation, come early for the good stuff.
LA's 1781 birthplace: marketplace stalls, taquitos at Cielito Lindo, mariachi on weekends — history you can snack through.
Three floors of automotive art behind that swooping ribbon facade — the Vault tour is worth the upgrade for any car-curious date.

nightlife.s: DTLA hip-hop room inside a 1920s bank — vault doors, big-name DJs, and a dance floor that actually dances.
Cahuenga Corridor club spinning hip-hop and reggaeton most nights of the week — unpretentious for Hollywood, built for dancing.
Long-running no-velvet-rope hip-hop and R&B bar off Cahuenga — DJs nightly and zero bottle-service attitude.
h.wood Group's surreal WeHo room where the hip-hop A-list actually shows up — Thursdays only and bottle-service-heavy, so bring a crew.
Hollywood's big-room club — mostly EDM heavyweights with occasional hip-hop bookings; check the calendar and go for the sound system.
Four-story Art Deco stock exchange turned dance cathedral — a DJ Mag Top 100 club with a floor that shakes.
Through a wardrobe into pre-revolution Havana: live Cuban bands, burlesque, and 100+ rums — the most transporting night out in LA.
Enter through a fridge into a 1970s house party — funk and classic-hits dance floor where strangers end up singing together.
Fifteenth-floor French rooftop with firepits and skyline views — live jazz early, DJs late; the DTLA date-night default.
Historic Black-owned dancehall (est. 1973) with five rooms running house, hip-hop, and R&B parties — LA dance-floor royalty.
Silver Lake's two-floor institution for cumbia, reggaeton, and underground parties — sweaty, cheap, and reliably fun.
Intimate listening room by LAX booking LA's best straight-ahead players — great cocktails, zero talkers, perfect late date.
Studio City's tiny 1970 fusion temple where session legends jam over giant stuffed potatoes — gloriously unchanged.
80s-themed hidden bar behind The Line Hotel — live cover sets, arcade games, and private karaoke rooms for the afterparty.
Koreatown's plush private-suite karaoke — huge English/Korean/Chinese songbook and bottle service until 2a.

eats.s: The 'Trust Me' set that democratized Nozawa's warm-rice sushi — DTLA outpost of the LA-born empire; no reservations, worth the wait.
The original hand roll bar — crackling nori, warm rice, toro-to-lobster in five bites; solo-counter-friendly and under $30.
Little Tokyo icon since 1980 — the lunch sashimi special is LA's most beloved deal; line up before 11:15a.
Michelin-starred Edomae omakase downtown — Chef Hiro's austere, seasonal 20-course flight for a proper occasion.
Ten seats hidden behind Sugarfish Beverly Hills — the full high-end expression of the Nozawa style without the scene.
Legendary strip-mall omakase above Sunset — no California rolls, no substitutions, just pristine fish and celebrity regulars.
West LA's polished sushi-and-omakase room — creative rolls named for industry regulars plus a serious traditional counter.
Nobu Matsuhisa's 1987 original — miso black cod and yellowtail jalapeño were invented in this unassuming room.
Sawtelle's tonkotsu-tsukemen destination — 60-hour broth worth every minute of the line; hit the Annex across the street.
Little Tokyo's perpetually-packed ramen counter — old-school shoyu-tonkotsu and chashu that built LA's ramen obsession.
Handmade udon pulled in the open kitchen — the sea-urchin cream udon is a Little Tokyo bucket-list bowl.
Echo Park's Michelin-starred sake bar — rare bottles, izakaya snacks, and staff who love walking beginners through the list.
Ototo's big sibling: refined seasonal izakaya cooking — the karaage and market-fish crudo anchor a great date dinner.
Koreatown's gold-standard KBBQ — prime beef, pro table service, and banchan that embarrass the all-you-can-eat joints.
The younger, louder KBBQ — quality meats, scene-y energy, and soju towers; ideal for a group night out.
24-hour K-town temple of galbi jjim on Western Ave — the cheese-torched short-rib cauldron is LA's best 1am decision.
Sherman Oaks family Thai gone national-best-restaurant famous — Thai Taco Tuesday is one of LA's great food events.
DTLA counter doing sharp, funky central-Thai cooking — boat noodles with real depth; casual enough for a first date.

chinese.s: The restaurant that made the SGV America's Sichuan capital — toothpick lamb and boiled fish in green-pepper broth; go early.
Chengdu Taste's great rival — refined mala classics like lamb in cumin and cold-pot skewers straight off a Chengdu street.
Chengdu Taste's noodle shop — mala-slick dan dan and sour-pork mian in a quick-hit San Gabriel storefront.
Rosemead's Michelin-recognized Cantonese palace — made-to-order dim sum that set the standard for the whole country.
Alhambra's Bib Gourmand dim sum heavyweight — oversized har gow and 100+ items, no carts, everything from the steamer.
Monterey Park classic still running old-school push-cart service — weekend banquet-hall chaos in the best way.
Home of the legendary Shandong beef roll — crispy pancake, cilantro, sweet bean sauce; a $15 SGV rite of passage.
Monterey Park's xian bing specialists — molten meat pies and zhajiang noodles, pure Beijing comfort food.
The SGV's beloved Taiwanese breakfast — fan tuan, salty soy milk, and fried crullers; dining room back open, mornings only.
The Taiwanese soup-dumpling empire's US flagship territory at Westfield Santa Anita — XLB folded 18 times, worth the wait.
China's service-obsessed hot pot giant in Arcadia — iPad ordering, hand-pulled noodle dances, and free manicures while you wait.

chinese.n: Half & Half Tea House 伴伴堂
chinese.s: SGV boba royalty — the honey boba milk tea with sea-salt cream that spawned a thousand imitators.
The San Gabriel Square flagship of America's biggest Chinese grocery — live seafood tanks, roast duck, and every Sichuan pantry staple.
The largest Buddhist temple in the Western Hemisphere — Tang-dynasty-style halls in the Hacienda Heights hills, with a vegetarian dining hall.
The 250-vendor Asian street-food mega-market at Santa Anita Park — 2026 runs Jun 19-21 and Aug 14-16, 3p-11p.
The longest-running Lunar New Year parade outside China — 127 years of lion dancers and firecrackers down Broadway every winter.

chinese.n: Monterey Park Lunar New Year Festival
chinese.s: The SGV's massive street festival — blocks of food stalls, lion dances, and rides in America's first suburban Chinatown each January/February.
Rowland Heights outpost of Taiwan's famous KTV chain — private suites, deep Mando/Canto songbook, open till 2a.
Chinatown's strawberry-cream-cake maker since 1938 — three generations of LA birthdays, plus almond cookies to go.

fishing.s: King Harbor's half-day workhorse for calico bass, rockfish, and summer bonito — easiest party-boat intro in the South Bay; CA license required aboard.

fishing.n: Marina del Rey Sportfishing (New Del Mar)
fishing.s: Closest landing to the city — half- and 3/4-day runs over the Santa Monica Bay reefs for calico, rockfish, and the odd yellowtail.
San Pedro's storied full fleet — 3/4-day boats work Catalina's front side for yellowtail and bass when the water warms.
Harbor-mouth landing with half-day and twilight trips — sand bass and sculpin close, rockfish limits in winter.
Quiet 1,310-ft concrete pier at Washington Blvd — halibut, perch, and mackerel; public piers need no CA license.
The horseshoe pier's deep water kicks up bonito and mackerel runs — license-free fishing plus fish markets when they're not biting.
San Pedro's 1,200-ft harbor pier off Cabrillo Beach — license-free, family-calm water, and lit for night sessions.
Miles of open sand for barred surfperch and summer corbina on sand crabs — shore fishing does require a CA license (16+), unlike the piers.
Trophy largemouth factory that's produced near-world-record bass — rent a skiff and work the points at dawn; license required.
Striped bass and largemouth in a dramatic I-5 canyon reservoir — troll the dam face early before the wakeboarders wake up.
The SGV's stocked 70-acre lake — winter trout plants and resident bass ten minutes from the 605; license required.

biking.s: Brentwood's shady canyon-bottom cruise under oaks and sycamores — reopened June 2025 after the Palisades Fire; check conditions before rolling.
Rolling oak-savanna singletrack in the Santa Monica Mountains NRA — smooth, social, and rattlesnake-sunny; the classic SoCal XC intro.
The Bulldog grind up to Castro Crest pays off with ocean-to-valley views and the M*A*S*H set on the way out — a proper leg-tester.
Whittier's punchy hillside network on the SGV's doorstep — tight switchbacks, ridge views, and a fast flowy return.
San Dimas lakeside loops with 14+ miles of buffed singletrack — beginner-friendly grades with enough punch to stay interesting.
The 11-mile urban-canyon classic just over the Orange County line — mellow, well-marked, and busy with friendly locals every weekend.
22 flat miles from Will Rogers to Torrance along the sand — the world's best paved recovery spin, with taco stops built in.

The Altadena classic: an 8.3-mile loop climbing Fern Truck Trail to a saddle with LA views, then dropping El Prieto's oak-canyon singletrack — exposure, tight switchbacks, drops, rock gardens and stream crossings. Start at the Windsor lot by JPL; run a bell and watch the poison oak.

biking.n: Aliso and Wood Canyons Wilderness Park
biking.s: 30-plus miles of official trail across 4,500 acres of coastal canyon wilderness between Laguna Niguel and Aliso Viejo. $3 parking off Alicia Parkway, open 7a to sunset; trails close for days after rain.

About 17 miles of graded road and singletrack over 2,500 acres of Foothill Ranch canyon, shared with hikers and horses — Red Rock Canyon itself is hikers-only. $3 parking at the Borrego lot on Portola Pkwy.

social.n: Salsa & Bachata at The Granada LA
social.s: Alhambra's three-floor Latin dance palace — salsa room, bachata room, hip-hop patio, with beginner classes before the social; 18+.
A 1950s Commerce steakhouse that turns into SoCal's friendliest salsa floor — free-flowing lessons then open dancing till late.
The Music Center's free plaza dance parties — a different style each week (salsa, disco, cumbia, Afrobeats) with beginner lessons; zero experience needed.

social.n: Motown on Mondays at The Short Stop
social.s: Echo Park's 13-year-strong Monday institution — no cover, soul and Motown all night, and the least intimidating dance floor in LA.
LA's most social run crew — Wednesday track nights at LACC draw 50+ runners of every pace, with food stops after.
Free sunrise workout with hugs and hill sprints at Griffith Observatory — relentlessly welcoming; show up once and you're a regular.
Playa del Rey's long-running swing night at the Elks Lodge — beginner Lindy lesson included, live bands often, all ages of dancers.
Weekly Mandarin/English conversation table in the San Gabriel Valley — half the room is practicing your language, so everyone talks.
Burbank's 21+ nerd bar with 200+ free board games, craft beer, and strangers who want to play Catan — Fri/Sat runs till 2a.

social.n: Jazz jam at The World Stage
social.s: Leimert Park's storied performance gallery — the weekly jam invites players and listeners into LA's deepest jazz lineage.
Drop-in coached beach volleyball on the Santa Monica courts — $20 sessions, all levels rotated together, instant social circle.
Free Wednesday trivia in a log-cabin bar in Los Feliz — teams up to six, beer prizes, and easy banter with neighboring tables.
ROW DTLA's Sunday open-air food market — dozens of vendors, communal tables, and the city's easiest low-stakes hang.

Sundays from 6:30p with Westside Soccer Best Pickup Big Goals, Goalies- Sat & Sun at Campus El Segundo Athletic Fields · no Meetup fee.

Sundays from 6:30p with Best Turf Pickup Big Goals, Goalies every Saturday & Sunday at Campus El Segundo Athletic Fields · no Meetup fee.

social.s: Join LA Societal "City of Angels" "Mix & Mingle" for a relaxed, beginner-friendly Pickleball & Mingling Mixer. Come for the games, stay to make new local friends. Saturdays from 8a with LA Societal City of Angels Mix & Mingle! at 6333 W 3rd St, Los Angeles, CA 90036 · no Meetup fee.

This is a moderately strenuous hike. The hikes are about 2 hours long and about 4 miles, and those miles include steep ascents and descents, most often on single track trails. We move at a fairly rapid pace. Saturdays from 3:30p with Los Angeles Hiking Group at Griffith Park Merry Go Round Lot 2, LOS ANGELES · no Meetup fee.

social.n: Saturday Afternoon Outdoor V-ball Meetup @ Victory Park
social.s: Saturdays from 1:30p with The Great Pasadena Volleyball Club at Victory Park, Pasadena · no Meetup fee.

social.n: Co-Ed Pickup Soccer Los Angeles (Exposition Park)
social.s: Saturdays from 4:50p with Los Angeles Co-Ed Pickup Soccer - Pezo at Exposition Park, Los Angeles · $11.99 on Meetup.

social.n: Sunday Afternoon Outdoor V-ball Meetup @ Victory Park
social.s: Sundays from 1:30p with The Great Pasadena Volleyball Club at Victory Park, Pasadena · no Meetup fee.

social.n: The Night Skate - Downtown Los Angeles
social.s: Meet: On 2nd/San Pedro Instagram or our Facebook Group are the best places for real time updates: Follow @thenightskatela on Instagram Or go to Time: We skate @ 8:08pm (promptly!) so if you are running a bit… Tuesdays from 8p with Southern California Urban Inline/Roller Skating at Weller Court, Los Angeles · no Meetup fee.

social.n: Cypress Park to the LA River 5K + Coffee
social.s: Join us for the first Cypress Park / Mt. Washington Run Club meetup. A relaxed neighborhood 5K from Cypress Park to the LA River, followed by optional coffee at 1802 Roasters. Sundays from 7a with Cypress Park / Mt. Washington Run Club at 1802 Coffee Roasters, Los Angeles · no Meetup fee.
Since they’re public lots, you’ll see QR codes for payment, but café customers can park for free. Saturdays from 9a with Japanese & English Chill Meetup at Awaken Cafe, Los Angeles · no Meetup fee.

Creativetoolkits is a community of 3D artists, fabricators, animators, VFX artists, TouchDesigner visual artists, software engineers, post-production professionals, videographers, directors, music producers… Saturdays from 3p with Creativetoolkits at Smalls LA Cafe & Market, Los Angeles · no Meetup fee.
Join us for trivia each Thursday evening on our rooftop terrace! Thursdays from 5:30p with West LA Tomat Rooftop Games, Trivia, & Music Meetup Group at Tomat, Los angeles · no Meetup fee.
Tuesdays from 8:30p with VibeCuratorGuide at Bar Lis, Los Angeles · no Meetup fee.

social.n: Board Games at The Original Farmers’ Market!
social.s: Bring Your Own Board Game (optional) and jacket (it gets chilly at night)! Come hang out, meet new people, and enjoy a chill game night on the second floor of The Farmers’ Market at The Grove. Fridays from 5:30p with Board Game and Brew Meetup at Farmers' Market, Los Angeles · no Meetup fee.
Fridays from 7p with Burbank Board Games Meetup Group at 1719 Grismer Ave, Burbank · no Meetup fee.

social.n: FTB weekly Language exchange(every Thursdays) TEMPORARILY AT BLOSSOM MARKET HALL
social.s: This is a weekly meet up that will occur every Thursdays in the City of San Gabriel. Thursdays from 6:30p with Eastern LA Japanese/English language exchange 東羅府郡日英交流會 at Blossom Market Hall, San Gabriel · no Meetup fee.

Join us to take a break from stressors, bring stillness to mind, move through the heart, and give yourself the time to recharge and restart. Sundays from 9:45a with Free Tai Chi for Beginners Los Angeles at Dr Paul Carlson Park, Culver City · no Meetup fee.
Come on by between 6:30-9:30 pm and play from our collection, or bring your own favorites. Wednesdays from 6:30p with Rock Coffee at ROCK Coffee House, Los Angeles · no Meetup fee.

remote.s: Worklounge on the 7th & 8th floors of 915 Wilshire Blvd in the Financial District. Wi-Fi, phone rooms and coffee & tea on every plan, on-site parking with EV charging, and private day offices from $59. Unlimited members get 7a–7p access and 150 prints/mo; the day pass is M–F 8:30a–5p.

The downtown WeWork, in South Park Center a few blocks from Crypto.com Arena. High-speed Wi-Fi, phone booths, business-class printers, bookable meeting rooms and lounges, plus a food hall, wellness room, parent's room and games in the building. Staffed on site, with member events.
remote.p: Day pass from $39 · coworking from $289/mo · dedicated desk from $342/mo

remote.s: Independent coworking on the 2nd floor (no elevator) of 1325 Palmetto St in the Arts District. Wi-Fi, coffee & tea, phone booths, conference rooms, a printer/scanner (19¢ b&w · 64¢ color), a kitchen, bike storage and leashed dogs welcome. Day pass covers the communal areas M–F 8a–4p; members get 24/7 access, and dedicated desks add the other California locations.
remote.p: $35 day pass · flex desk $400/mo · dedicated desk $650/mo
remote.b: Reviewers call it clean and quiet, a good place to study

remote.s: 25,000 sq ft space at 929 Colorado Ave, two blocks from the E Line's Downtown Santa Monica terminus. High-speed Wi-Fi, specialty coffee & tea, kitchen, phone booths, print/scan and gopod call pods ($30/hr); hot desks $75/day, meeting rooms from $40/hr. Day passes run 9a–5p; WorkCafé members get 24/7 access. Street and city-structure parking.
remote.b: Big events (e.g. LA Tech Week) fill the floor and get noisy

remote.s: 10,000 sq ft at 9415 Culver Blvd in downtown Culver City, a 10-min walk from the E Line. Open WorkCafé lounge, hot desks ($75/day), gopod call pods (≈$30/hr) and meeting rooms (≈$60–80/hr). Front desk M–F 9a–5p for day passes; members on 24/7 plans badge in anytime. Metered street parking or the Culver Steps garage; leashed dogs welcome.
remote.b: Reviewers call it quiet; phone booths can be hard to find

remote.s: The Goodhue landmark at 630 W 5th St. Wi-Fi throughout, ~255 free public computers, in-building laptop loans and mobile print upload. Glass study rooms in Literature (Upper Level 3) and Business (Lower Level 1): library card needed, 2 hr per floor, book in person same day or a day ahead. Mon–Thu 10–8, Fri–Sat 9:30–5:30, Sun 1–5. Parking lot and bike racks.
remote.p: Free (printing 25¢ b&w · 50¢ color, $6.25/day free with a card)
remote.b: Weekday mornings calmest; weekends busier with events

remote.s: 601 Santa Monica Blvd, downtown Santa Monica. Free Wi-Fi, plus 18 reservable one-person laptop tables (4-hr sessions, outlets) and seven study rooms (2 hr) on the 2nd floor, all free with an SMPL card — book online up to a day ahead. Laptops can be borrowed with a reservation. Mon–Thu 10–8, Sat 10–5. Paid parking in the library structure off 7th St.
remote.b: Quiet corners but some sections noisy; private study rooms need booking

remote.s: Modern teahouse in Mandarin Plaza, 970 N Broadway in Chinatown: fast Wi-Fi, big tables and a large outdoor patio. Daytime is for tea and laptops; Thu–Sat evenings it turns into Steep After Dark, a tea-cocktail bar, so plan to pack up by late afternoon.
remote.b: Calm teahouse by day; after 5p it turns into a cocktail bar

remote.s: Airy roaster-café at 1019 S Santa Fe Ave in the Arts District, with Wi-Fi, a spacious communal table that works for in-person meetings, and free street parking — rare downtown.
remote.b: Often crowded; weekends get busy and seats are hard to find

remote.s: Espresso bar at 855 S Broadway in the Broadway theater district, with plenty of outlets inside and a curbside patio — a good base between Central Library and the Fashion District.
remote.b: Lots of seating inside and out; lively; weekdays best for patio seats

events.s: Tyler, the Creator's two-day carnival and festival on the Dodger Stadium grounds. This year's lineup includes Future, Don Toliver, Steve Lacy and Turnstile. Gates open at noon both days.

The zoo after dark, lit up for the holidays. This year's nature theme has glowing birds, butterflies, marine life and Ice Age giants. It runs on select evenings only (closed 11/26, 11/30, 12/1, 12/7, 12/14–16, 12/24–25, 12/31 and 1/4–7), and tickets start at $19.
Thanksgiving Eve football at SoFi Stadium, streaming on Netflix.

The 94th edition of the Sunday-after-Thanksgiving parade, with marching bands, floats, celebrities and Santa on the U-shaped loop of Hollywood Blvd, Vine and Sunset. The 2026 start time isn't posted yet; last year's parade began at 6p.
Thursday Night Football at SoFi Stadium: the Rams host Kansas City (Prime Video).

events.n: Victoria Monét: Frequency of Love Tour
events.s: The three-time Grammy-winning R&B singer brings her new album's tour to the YouTube Theater at Hollywood Park.

LA Ballet's Nutcracker opens at UCLA's Royce Hall (Dec 11–13), then moves to the Dolby Theatre in Hollywood with the Los Angeles Ballet Orchestra (Dec 18–27). There's a sensory-friendly matinee on 12/26.
The Mandopop superstar plays one arena night at the Kia Forum, a highlight of the year for Chinese-pop fans in LA.
The a cappella group's holiday tour stops at the Kia Forum three days before Christmas.
The NBA's Christmas showcase in LA: LeBron James returns to Crypto.com Arena with Philadelphia to face Luka's Lakers (ABC/ESPN). Buy only through Ticketmaster, the Lakers' official seller.

events.n: 128th Golden Dragon Parade 金龙大游行
events.s: Chinatown's Lunar New Year parade welcomes the Year of the Goat (羊): lion and dragon dancers, firecrackers and floats. The loop runs from Hill & Temple up Broadway and Bernard. The theme is "Unity in the Community."
The Clippers host Oklahoma City at Intuit Dome in Inglewood. Tip-off 7:30p, doors at 6p; tickets via Ticketmaster.
Ten days of new models, EVs and test drives at the LA Convention Center downtown. Mostly 9a–10p on weekends, shorter hours midweek and on Thanksgiving; tickets online only.
A walk-through Christmas light maze at Santa Anita Park with a holiday village, ice skating and rides (add-ons extra). Timed arrival windows; admission from $29, varying by date.
Steve Lacy brings his Oh Yeah? tour to the Hollywood Bowl for a hometown headline show of R&B-leaning guitar pop. Gates 6:30p, show 8p.

events.n: Enchanted: Forest of Light at Descanso Gardens
events.s: Descanso Gardens' nighttime holiday light walk through the gardens. Timed entry every 30 min from 5:30–8:30p, open till 10p; advance tickets only, adults about $29–52 by date.
The Kings host Anaheim at Crypto.com Arena on Thanksgiving weekend, the home half of the Freeway Faceoff after the 11/27 game in Anaheim.
Sunday Night Football at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood as the Chargers host New England. Kickoff 5:20p PT on NBC.

events.n: Stevie Wonder: Songs in the Key of Life 50th
events.s: Stevie Wonder performs his 1976 album Songs in the Key of Life in full for its 50th anniversary at Intuit Dome. 8p; tickets about $300–500.

events.n: Take the train to LA: Urban Hike in Pasadena
events.s: Part of Colorado Boulevard in Pasadena will be closed to traffic on Sunday, November 15, 2026 from 9AM to 3PM, so people can ride bikes on the streets. Sunday from 9:21a with Sunrise to Sunset Hikers at Pasadena Memorial Park · no Meetup fee.

events.n: Flat Top to Paradise Hill to Peanut Lake Hike
events.s: Join us, as we hike to Lincoln Heights, El Serreno and Montecito Heights! We will go to Flat Top,Lincoln Heights Hill Top View, Paradise Hill, and finally to Peanut Lake in Deb’s Park! Sunday from 9:15a with Los Angeles Hiking Group at Hillside Elementary School, Los Angeles · no Meetup fee.

events.n: Borrego Canyon Trail to Red Rock Canyon Hiking
events.s: Tuesday from 10a with Sunday Hike Los Angeles at Starbucks Wilshire Union Center, Los angeles · no Meetup fee.

events.n: MONTEREY PARK: Sichuanese Dinner at Cui Hua Lou Szechuan
events.s: Reminder, their food is not as spicy as other Sichuanese places, but the flavors are great. Sunday from 5p with Eating the SGV (San Gabriel Valley) + Beyond at Cui Hua Lou, Monterey Park · no Meetup fee.

events.n: Funtastic Hike at Culver City and Kenneth Hahn Park. Moderate Paced!
events.s: Let’s enjoy a moderate paced hike together at Culver City Park to Kenneth Hahn Park. This is a great chance to get some fresh air, exercise, and meet new people who enjoy the outdoors. Sunday from 9a with ¡ ᗯᗩᑎteᗪ To ᗪo Tᕼᗩt . . . ᒍᑌᔕt ᑎot ᗩᒪoᑎe ! ! ! ℠ at Bill Botts Field, Culver City · no Meetup fee.
Saturday from 7:30p with Latin Dance Mixer & Meetup at 1618 Cotner Avenue, Los Angeles · no Meetup fee.

events.n: Evening Conditioning Hike in La Cañada
events.s: We'll enjoy great views of the LA basin and the night sky while getting an aerobic workout. Thursday from 6:45p with Sierra Club Pasadena Group - Hikes and More! at Palm Crest Elementary School, La Cañada Flintridge · no Meetup fee.

Join us on a beautiful bicycle ride through the city of Roses for the next Cyclvia which is returning to the SG valley after a long hiatus. Sunday from 9a with Southern California Cycling Group at 419 South Euclid Avenue, Pasadena · no Meetup fee.

iceskating.s: Downtown Santa Monica's outdoor rink (formerly Ice at Santa Monica) at 5th St and Arizona Ave, a block from Third Street Promenade. The 2026–27 season opened Thu Nov 5, with hours Mon–Fri 3–10p and noon–10p on weekends and holidays. Admission is $22 with skates, and lockers are $5. The closing date isn't posted yet.

iceskating.n: LA Kings Holiday Ice at L.A. Live
iceskating.s: The Kings' seasonal outdoor rink on Peacock Place, in front of Crypto.com Arena and a short hop from the rest of downtown. The 2026–27 LA Kings Holiday Ice Festival runs Nov 27, 2026–Jan 3, 2027. Prices for this season aren't posted yet, so check before going, and pair it with a game night at the arena.

Burbank's rink, open since 1961 and run by the Kings group since 2019. Public skate comes in 90-minute blocks: weekdays from 2:30 or 3p, Sat 6–7:30p and Sun 3:45–5:15p. It's $22 at the door or $18 booked online, with skates included, and skate aides rent for $15. Hockey sticks, pucks and headphones aren't allowed on public sessions.

The rink at 300 E Green St in central Pasadena runs public sessions every day: Mon–Tue 1–3p, longer Wed–Fri afternoons, and evening skates Thu 7:30–9p and Fri–Sat 8–10p. Admission is $17 plus $5 rental, with $2 off for Pasadena residents and seniors, and an 18+ Lunch Bunch session costs $21. Tickets are sold at the door only.

The Zamboni family's rink, opened in 1940, the rink that led Frank Zamboni to invent his ice resurfacer. The Kings group bought it in 2022 and remodeled it. Public skate is $18.50 for ages 7 and up, $16.60 for kids 6 and under, $16.50 for seniors, military and students. Rental skates are free and no reservation is needed.

The El Segundo rink near LAX, part of the LA Kings rink group, with public skating between team and league ice. Admission is $16.75 for adults, $15.75 for kids 12 and under, and $12.50 for seniors, military, students or the last hour. Rentals are $9.75, in figure or hockey styles. Check the rink's online calendar for session times.

iceskating.n: The Cube Ice and Entertainment Center
iceskating.s: Santa Clarita's rink in Valencia runs public sessions 1:30–4:30p every day, weekday mornings 9–11a and 7:30–9:30p on three evenings. Admission with skates is $21, or $16 without; weekday mornings are $17, and seniors 55+ pay $12 with skates. Some sessions move to The Pond, the second rink.

Artesia's rink posts public sessions most afternoons, usually 2:15–4:15p and longer on some days, plus Friday and Saturday evening skates such as Sat 5:45–9:30p. Admission is $15 ($14 for age 10 and under) plus $5 rental. The rink runs in the low-to-mid 50s in winter, so bring a jacket and gloves.

skating.s: Venice has billed itself as the roller-skating capital of the world since the late '70s, and the city still runs a public skate plaza on the boardwalk by the rec center at 1800 Ocean Front Walk, open daily. It's LA's best-known place to watch skaters or join in, with the beach bike path alongside and the 16,000 sq ft concrete skatepark next door.

TrailLink lists the 22-mile asphalt-and-concrete beach path from Will Rogers to Torrance for inline skating. Start at Santa Monica Pier: Venice is 1.8 mi south, where the bike path splits from the pedestrian promenade. It detours onto streets around Marina del Rey, and blown sand can bury stretches (a reviewer found one impassable in Feb 2026).

7.4 miles of car-free asphalt along the river from Victory Blvd at the Burbank–Glendale line, past Griffith Park and Atwater Village, down to Egret Park in Elysian Valley. It's the closest long skate to downtown, with pocket parks (Marsh, Steelhead, Sunnynook) for breaks and the Baum bike bridge at Los Feliz Blvd.

A 4.3-mile concrete beach path from Shoreline Marina to Belmont Shore. It's 17 ft wide, with separate 6-ft bike lanes and a 5-ft walking lane, so skaters get room, and it passes Belmont Pier with views of the port cranes and Palos Verdes. Reviewers praise the upkeep but say it's busy even early in the morning.

6.4 miles of asphalt and concrete down the creek channel from Syd Kronenthal Park in Culver City to the beach path at Marina del Rey. Riders call it functional rather than pretty, with concrete walls most of the way, and the park entrance is a steep ramp, so save legs for the climb back. The park has free 4-hour parking and restrooms.

skating.n: San Gabriel River Trail (Seal Beach end)
skating.s: A fully paved 39-mile channel path from the mountains to the sea. The part worth skating is the south end, from River's End Park in Seal Beach up toward Los Alamitos. A reviewer who has skated it for 40 years warns of speeding motorized bikes lately, and north of Bellflower it turns industrial, with camps and trash. Go early and stay south.

Glendale's rink still skates on the solid-maple floor laid in 1956. Sessions run Sat 10a–noon, Sat–Sun 1:30–4p and 8–11p, plus an 18+ night Mon 8–11p. Evenings are $23 online, weekend afternoons $18, rental $8. Your own inlines are welcome if the wheels pass the rink's floor-safety check (no exposed bolts).

Free open-streets Sundays that hand miles of LA streets to walkers, bikes and skaters for the day. The organizers list roller skates among the welcome wheels and require helmets for skaters under 18. Next up is CicLAvia Pasadena, Sun Nov 15, 2026, 9a–3p; each route is posted on the site ahead of the day.
